moat_against: Commodity input costs (pork bellies, beef, turkey, nuts) cannot be fully or quickly passed through — FY2025 gross margin fell to 15.6% from 17.0%
ROIC proxy fell from 17-21% (FY2016-19) to 8-10% (FY2021-24) and 5.1% in impairment-hit FY2025 — returns no longer clear the cost of capital by a wide margin
Private label and cautious consumers: Retail volume fell ~9% in Q3 FY2026, organic net sales -2% in the quarter
Capital allocation scars: $3.35B Planters acquisition (2021) followed by Retail intangible impairments in FY2025; International minority investments impaired in both FY2025 and FY2026
Protein category exposure to changing consumer tastes and GLP-1-era demand shifts; no structural cost advantage over larger packaged-food peers
moat_for: Durable branded portfolio with real shelf presence: SPAM, Skippy, Planters, Jennie-O, Applegate, Columbus, Hormel chili and pepperoni
Foodservice channel strength — 12th consecutive quarter of organic net sales growth in Q3 FY2026, premium prepared proteins and branded pepperoni
Scale in value-added protein processing and long-standing retail/foodservice relationships; 60 consecutive years of dividend increases signals franchise durability
Pricing actions taken in FY2025-26 are sticking on an adjusted basis: FY2026 YTD adjusted operating margin +30bp, adjusted EPS +6% through Q3
moat_justification: Moderate/narrow moat (5/10): genuine brands and foodservice relationships, but commodity-cost pass-through is incomplete, gross margin has eroded from ~20%+ (FY2016-19) to 15.6-17.4% over the last five fiscal years, and the ROIC proxy has fallen from 17-21% to 8-10% (5.1% in FY2025) — returns now sit near, not well above, the cost of capital, so no score above the moderate band is justified.
name: Hormel Foods Corporation
one_liner: Durable branded-protein franchise, moat 5/10 with eroding margins and ROIC — does not clear 15% at $20.28 (weighted IRR 9.2%, IV@15% $10.94); it would clear 15% only near $10.94.
